primitives.name: Zero-Shot Cross-Modal Retrieval
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT **Rationale:** bind NGS tracking, broadcast video, commentary audio, and injury-report text into ONE shared embedding space via image-paired contrastive learning, so zero-shot cross-modal retrieval (e.g., text query → tracking clips) works without any paired tracking-text data; needs adaptation (modality encoders for trajectories, NFL-scale data).

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of ImageBind is symmetric InfoNCE loss over image-paired modality pairs. This constrains embeddings such that similar modalities align under a shared image anchor. The mathematical structure ensures that even without direct (M1, M2) pairs, their embeddings become aligned through the common image space. The emergent alignment is a consequence of the shared anchor, which acts as a bridge. In GSI, this enables probabilistic inference over modalities like text and audio to predict game events. In GSE, it supports state transitions by aligning tracking trajectories with other modalities. The failure mode occurs when image anchors are noisy or when modalities do not naturally pair with images, leading to degraded alignment quality.
